mat_help_baseline: Eclipse Memory Analyzer OQL help (help.eclipse.org latest)
honesty: Only cases with equivalency=mat-referenced may close a MAT compatibility-matrix row. Cases labeled non-equivalency are Mnemosyne bounds or syntax deltas and must not support equivalency claims.

mat_refs.section: FROM Clause — by the object addresses of more than one class

cases.syntax_note: MAT documents comma-separated class object addresses/ids. Mnemosyne ships comma-separated quoted class-name patterns with the same multi-source union + ID-dedup intent.

mat_refs.section: SELECT Clause — Flatten select items into an object list (OBJECTS)
FROM Clause — sub select with SELECT OBJECTS s.value

cases.query: SELECT OBJECTS n.parent FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count = 1
SELECT OBJECTS n.parent.link FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count = 1
SELECT OBJECTS n.parent.link.target FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count = 1

cases.non_equivalency_reason: Mnemosyne hard-caps SELECT OBJECTS field hops at 3. MAT OQL help does not document this hop bound; this case freezes the Mnemosyne grammar boundary only.

mat_refs.section: SELECT Clause — without DISTINCT OBJECTS, duplicate class rows are retained

cases.syntax_note: MAT documents that OBJECTS without DISTINCT keeps duplicate rows when many sources map to the same target. Mnemosyne matches that non-DISTINCT duplicate retention for SELECT OBJECTS.
cases.query: SELECT OBJECTS n.parent FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count >= 3 AND count < 5

mat_refs.section: SELECT Clause — Select unique objects (DISTINCT OBJECTS)

cases.syntax_note: MAT DISTINCT OBJECTS collapses duplicate projected targets by object identity. Mnemosyne ships the same collapse for SELECT DISTINCT OBJECTS only; SELECT DISTINCT * / field lists remain unsupported (named bound).
cases.query: SELECT DISTINCT OBJECTS n.parent FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count >= 3 AND count < 5

cases.non_equivalency_reason: Mnemosyne bounds DISTINCT to OBJECTS projection only (SELECT DISTINCT * / field lists rejected). MAT supports broader DISTINCT; this case freezes the Mnemosyne grammar boundary and must not support equivalency claims.

expect.error_contains: DISTINCT is only supported with OBJECTS

mat_refs.section: SELECT Clause / OBJECTS — null field projections are skipped (no fabricated rows)

cases.query: SELECT OBJECTS n.parent FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE depth = 10

cases.non_equivalency_reason: Structured missing-field error is a Mnemosyne contract; MAT GUI behavior may differ. Does not close an equivalency matrix row.
Cycle-safe hop traversal with row omission is a Mnemosyne safety bound; not a recorded MAT golden result. Non-equivalency.
cases.query: SELECT OBJECTS n.parent.link FROM "com.example.Node" WHERE count = 1

cases.non_equivalency_reason: Explicit LIMIT truncation is a Mnemosyne result budget. MAT OQL BNF does not define LIMIT; this case does not support MAT equivalency claims.
Named M22 gap: eval(...) / Java expression execution remains explicitly unsupported.
